candidates: Avoid `forEach(async (item) => { ... })` when sequential execution is intended; this pattern fires all iterations concurrently and silently discards the returned Promises, causing interleaved output and no ordering or error-propagation guarantees. Use `for (const item of list) { await ... }` instead, and ensure any accompanying code comments accurately reflect whether execution is sequential or parallel.

When refactoring code into a conditional branch, audit for dead-code fragments — especially conditional expressions (ternaries, logical operators) that test a variable already known to be a fixed value within that branch. Simplify or remove the expression to reflect the actual runtime state and avoid misleading future readers.
